definitions.explanation: A single-wheeled pedal vehicle ridden for recreation or performance. A common activity in Japanese elementary schools.
A single-wheeled cart pushed by hand, used for carrying loads at construction sites, gardens, and farms.

examples.japanese: {一輪車|いちりんしゃ}に{乗|の}れる。
{小学校|しょうがっこう}の{休|やす}み{時間|じかん}に{一輪車|いちりんしゃ}で{遊|あそ}んだ。
examples.english: I played on a unicycle during recess at elementary school.

examples.japanese: サーカスの{道化師|どうけし}が{一輪車|いちりんしゃ}に{乗|の}りながらジャグリングをしていた。
examples.english: A circus clown was juggling while riding a unicycle.

examples.japanese: {一輪車|いちりんしゃ}で{土|つち}を{運|はこ}ぶ。
{工事現場|こうじげんば}で{一輪車|いちりんしゃ}を{押|お}している{作業員|さぎょういん}がいた。
examples.english: There was a worker pushing a wheelbarrow at the construction site.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{手入|てい}れに{一輪車|いちりんしゃ}があると{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: A wheelbarrow is handy for garden maintenance.

notes:
USAGE:
{一輪車|いちりんしゃ} has two distinct meanings depending on context. In everyday conversation, especially among children and families, it usually means unicycle. In construction or gardening contexts, it means wheelbarrow.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Unicycle riding is a common activity at Japanese elementary schools. Many schools have unicycles available for students to use during recess, and some hold unicycle competitions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一輪車|いちりんしゃ}に{乗|の}る (to ride a unicycle)
- {一輪車|いちりんしゃ}で{運|はこ}ぶ (to carry with a wheelbarrow)
- {一輪車|いちりんしゃ}を{押|お}す (to push a wheelbarrow)
